Support people with policy, training, and feedback.
screens.callout: Adoption is a business and people change, not only a tool launch.

screens.title: Module 11 review: safe agents
screens.lead: Systems that can act need strict access, evidence, and recovery controls.
bullets: Use least privilege.
Define allowed and denied actions.
Add human approval gates.
Test unusual and failure cases.
Keep logs, stop rules, and recovery steps.
screens.callout: Stopping safely is part of successful automation.

screens.title: CIDI prompt quick guide
screens.lead: Use these four parts, then review the result.

cards.title: Context
cards.body: Who you are, the situation, and the purpose.

cards.title: Instruction
cards.body: The clear action you want the AI to take.

cards.title: Details
cards.body: Audience, format, tone, limits, checks, and examples.

cards.title: Input
cards.body: The approved source material the AI should use.

screens.title: Privacy traffic light
screens.lead: When workplace policy is stricter, follow the policy.

cards.title: Green
cards.body: Public or approved low-risk information. Still check the output.

cards.title: Yellow
cards.body: Internal information. Use only with approval and proper controls.

cards.title: Red
cards.body: Secrets, regulated data, or highly sensitive records. Do not use in an unapproved tool.

screens.title: Source verification checklist
screens.lead: Use this before relying on research or factual claims.
bullets: Open the original source.
Check author, publisher, date, and version.
Read the exact supporting section.
Check place, group, units, and time period.
Record what the source does not prove.
screens.callout: If the source cannot be found or does not support the claim, remove or rewrite the claim.

screens.title: Output quality checklist
screens.lead: Use this before sending, presenting, or publishing AI-assisted work.
bullets: Correct: facts, calculations, names, and dates are checked.
Complete: the task and required parts are covered.
Clear: the audience can understand the result.
Safe: private data, rights, fairness, and risk are handled.
Owned: a responsible person approved the final use.
screens.callout: Quality is more than grammar and appearance.

screens.title: Data and chart checklist
screens.lead: Use this before a number becomes part of a decision.
bullets: Source, fields, units, and dates are clear.
Blanks, repeats, and outliers were reviewed.
Formula ranges and denominators were checked.
A second check supports the result.
The chart uses fair labels and scales.
screens.callout: Show assumptions and uncertainty beside the result.

screens.title: Pilot and ROI checklist
screens.lead: Use this before recommending a larger rollout.
bullets: The business problem and owner are clear.
A baseline and balanced measures exist.
The pilot has limits, thresholds, and stop rules.
Full cost and testable benefits are shown.
Risk, people, policy, training, and support are included.
screens.callout: A pilot is meant to create evidence, including evidence that the idea should stop.

screens.title: Agent safety checklist
screens.lead: Use this before software is allowed to take action.
bullets: Goal, scope, and definition of done are clear.
Access follows least privilege.
High-impact actions require approval.
Normal, edge, failure, and abuse cases were tested.
Logs, stop rules, and recovery are ready.
screens.callout: Do not connect a test agent to valuable systems or real secrets.

Answer three new workplace scenarios without notes, then check your reasoning.
selfCheck: All twelve modules have a plain-language summary.
Weak areas link to specific learning screens.
Scenario answers include evidence, risk, and human responsibility.

assignments.title: Homework 1: Tested Prompt Portfolio
instructions: Choose one safe, useful workplace task.
Submit the first prompt and output.
Show your CIDI revision, checks, corrected output, and final decision.
Explain in 150 to 300 words what improved and what still needs human review.
checklist: Task and audience are clear.
No unapproved private information is included.
First and revised versions are labeled.
Checks and human decision are visible.

assignments.title: Homework 2: Workplace Communication Package
instructions: Create one email and one short report section from approved or fictional source notes.
State the audience, purpose, tone, and action for each.
Submit source notes, AI-assisted drafts, your corrections, and final versions.
checklist: Both items trace back to source notes.
Tone and detail fit the audience.
Facts, privacy, promises, and authority were checked.
Final versions show human ownership.

assignments.title: Homework 3: Data Decision Brief
instructions: Prepare a small supplied, public, or approved dataset.
Show one checked calculation and one suitable chart.
Write a one-page brief that separates evidence, meaning, recommendation, and limits.
checklist: Headings, units, dates, and missing values are clear.
The calculation was checked a second way.
The chart answers one named question.
The recommendation does not overstate the evidence.

assignments.title: Homework 4: Safe Automation Plan
instructions: Map one repeated workflow that could use limited automation.
Document inputs, tools, permissions, approvals, logs, failure cases, and recovery.
Submit the workflow map and a short test report.
checklist: The simplest safe automation level was chosen.
Permissions are limited.
High-impact actions require approval.
Normal, edge, failure, and misuse cases are tested.

assignments.title: Capstone: Project Brief and Proposal
instructions: Choose one small business problem or repeated task.
Describe the current process, users, approved information, desired result, and why the problem matters.
Propose one limited AI-assisted improvement and name the human owner.
List early measures, risks, limits, and evidence you plan to collect.
checklist: The problem is specific and small enough to test.
The proposal names users, data, and human ownership.
Success measures and stop rules are included.

assignments.title: Capstone: Working File and Evidence
instructions: Collect your approved inputs, prompts or workflow, outputs, checks, corrections, and decisions.
Record time, cost, quality, risk, and user feedback from the test.
Explain failures and changes instead of hiding them.
checklist: Evidence is dated and organized.
Important claims can be checked.
Corrections and failed tests are visible.
Private information is removed or approved.

assignments.title: Capstone: Final Submission
instructions: Submit a clear summary of the problem, current process, proposed improvement, test, results, risks, controls, cost, value, and next recommendation.
Include your evidence appendix and a short guide another person could follow.
State what AI did, what people did, and who owns the final decision.
checklist: The result answers the original business problem.
Evidence supports the claimed value.
Risks, limits, approvals, and recovery are clear.
The package can be understood without the full ebook.

assignments.title: Capstone Presentation
instructions: Prepare a 7 to 10 minute presentation.
Explain the problem, evidence, design, test, result, risk controls, human role, and next step.
Be ready to answer questions and show one key artifact.
checklist: The story is clear and within time.
Claims match the submitted evidence.
The human decision and limits are explicit.
Slides or visuals are readable and accessible.
